# MQTT tools: MQTT Explorer, MQTTX & Mosquitto CLI

MQTT is the publish/subscribe protocol behind most IoT products: sensors, smart-home devices, vehicle telemetry, industrial equipment. Devices don't call each other. They publish messages to **topics** on a **broker**, and anyone subscribed to those topics receives them. To test such a system you need a client that can subscribe and see everything, publish crafted messages, and inspect flags such as QoS, retain and Last Will. This chapter covers three free tools that complement each other: **MQTT Explorer** for seeing the whole topic tree, **MQTTX** for precise multi-client scenarios, and **mosquitto_pub / mosquitto_sub** for scripts and CI.

| Key fact | MQTT Explorer | MQTTX | Mosquitto CLI |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Type** | Desktop GUI | Desktop GUI, also CLI and web | Command line |
| **Platforms** | Windows, macOS, Linux | Windows, macOS, Linux | Windows, macOS, Linux |
| **Strength** | Topic tree, history, diffs, retained-message cleanup | Several connections side by side, MQTT 5, Last Will | Scriptable, tiny, ideal for CI and reproductions |
| **Install** | mqtt-explorer.com (stores, `.exe`, `.dmg`, AppImage, snap) | mqttx.app | `apt install mosquitto-clients`, `brew install mosquitto`, Windows installer |

Public test brokers (no account needed): `test.mosquitto.org`, `broker.hivemq.com` and `broker.emqx.io`, all on port `1883` for plain MQTT.

```diagram
Device / service ──publish──► Broker ──deliver──► every subscriber of a matching topic
                     ▲                     │
     test client publishes crafted      test client subscribes to # or a prefix
     messages (QoS, retain, LWT)        and checks what arrives, when and how often
```

## MQTT essentials for testers: topics, wildcards, QoS, retain and Last Will

**Topics** are UTF-8 strings split into levels by `/`, for example `factory/line1/sensor42/temperature`. They are case-sensitive and created on first use.

| Wildcard (subscribe only) | Matches | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `+` | Exactly one level | `factory/+/sensor42/temperature` |
| `#` | Any number of levels, must be last | `factory/line1/#` |
| `$SYS/#` | Broker statistics (on brokers that provide them, such as Mosquitto) | `$SYS/broker/clients/connected` |

**QoS (Quality of Service)** is set per publish and per subscription. The delivered level is the lower of the two.

| QoS | Guarantee | Packets on the wire |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | At most once. May be lost | PUBLISH |
| 1 | At least once. May be duplicated | PUBLISH → PUBACK |
| 2 | Exactly once | PUBLISH → PUBREC → PUBREL → PUBCOMP |

- **Retained message:** a publish with the **retain** flag is stored by the broker as the topic's "last known value". Every *new* subscriber receives it immediately. To delete it, publish an empty retained message to the same topic.
- **Last Will and Testament (LWT):** when a client connects, it can register a *will* message. The broker publishes it if the client disappears **without** a clean DISCONNECT (crash, power loss, network drop). This is the usual way to implement `online` / `offline` status.
- **Session:** with *clean session = false* (MQTT 3.1.1) or *clean start = false* plus a session expiry interval (MQTT 5), the broker keeps subscriptions and queues QoS 1/2 messages while the client is offline, as long as the client reconnects with the **same client ID**.
- **Client ID:** must be unique per broker. A second connection with the same ID kicks the first one off. That's a classic source of "random disconnect" bugs.

## MQTT Explorer: browse the topic tree, publish and diff

1. Download MQTT Explorer from mqtt-explorer.com and start it. The connection dialog opens.
2. Enter a **Name**, choose the protocol `mqtt://`, and enter **Host** `test.mosquitto.org` and **Port** `1883`. Add **Username** / **Password** and turn on **Encryption (tls)** if your broker needs them.
3. Click **Advanced** to see the subscriptions. By default MQTT Explorer subscribes to `#` and `$SYS/#`. On a busy public broker, replace `#` with your own prefix, for example `gimmejob/qa-lab/#`. You can also set the **Client ID** here.
4. Click **Connect**. Topics appear as a tree on the left. Numbers show how many sub-topics and messages each branch has, and branches flash when new messages arrive.
5. Click a topic to see its **Value** on the right: payload, QoS, retain flag, and the time it was received. JSON is pretty-printed.
6. Open **History** under the value to see previous messages. Use the **diff** view to compare the current payload with the previous one, which is ideal for spotting the one field that changed.
7. Numeric topics can be plotted as a chart, which is useful for sensors that drift or spike.
8. In **Publish**, enter a topic and payload (raw, JSON or XML), choose **QoS**, tick **retain** if needed, and click **Publish**.
9. To remove a stale retained value, select the topic and click the delete (trash) button. MQTT Explorer can delete a single topic or a whole branch recursively.

![MQTT Explorer topic tree, message value and publish panel](https://mqtt-explorer.com/img/screen-composite.png "MQTT Explorer project screenshot: the topic tree with message details and history.")

> **Caveat:** Subscribing to `#` on a large production broker can flood the app and the network. Always narrow the subscription to the part of the tree you're testing.

## MQTTX: connections, subscriptions, Last Will and MQTT 5

MQTTX (by EMQ) keeps several connections open in one window. You can be "the device" in one tab and "the backend" in another.

1. Start MQTTX and click **New Connection** (`Ctrl/Cmd+N`) or **+** in the left sidebar. **Try public broker** creates a ready connection to `broker.emqx.io:1883`.
2. Fill in **Name**, **Client ID** (click refresh to generate one), **Host** with a protocol (`mqtt://`, `mqtts://`, `ws://`, `wss://`) and **Port** (`1883` plain, `8883` TLS, `8083` WebSocket, `8084` secure WebSocket on EMQX).
3. Open **Advanced** to set **MQTT Version** (5.0 by default, or 3.1.1 / 3.1), **Keep Alive**, **Clean Start** (MQTT 5) or **Clean Session** (MQTT 3.x), and automatic reconnect.
4. In **Last Will and Testament**, enter **Last-Will-Topic** (for example `gimmejob/qa-lab/device1/status`), **Last-Will-Payload** (`offline`), and the QoS and retain values. QoS defaults to 0 and retain to false.
5. Click **Connect** in the upper right corner.
6. Click **New Subscription**, enter a topic such as `gimmejob/qa-lab/#`, and pick a color. Separate several topics with commas.
7. In the publish area at the bottom, enter the topic, choose **QoS** and **Retain**, choose a payload format (**JSON**, **Plaintext**, **Base64**, **Hex**...), type the payload, and press **Send** or `Ctrl/Cmd+Enter`.
8. Received messages appear on the left and sent messages on the right. Click a subscription to filter the list to that topic.

![MQTTX Last Will and Testament settings](https://mqttx.app/images/mqttx-willmessage.png "Official MQTTX documentation screenshot: Last Will and Testament settings in a new connection.")

![MQTTX main window with subscriptions and messages](https://mqttx.app/images/mqttx-main.png "Official MQTTX documentation screenshot: the main window with subscriptions, received and published messages.")

> **QA tip:** Create two connections with **different client IDs**: `device-sim` with a Last Will, and `backend-observer` subscribed to the status topic. Then disconnect `device-sim` in different ways and watch what the observer receives.

## Mosquitto CLI: mosquitto_sub and mosquitto_pub

```bash
# Subscribe to a whole branch and print the topic in front of each message (-v)
mosquitto_sub -h test.mosquitto.org -t 'gimmejob/qa-lab/#' -v

# Publish one message with QoS 1
mosquitto_pub -h test.mosquitto.org -t 'gimmejob/qa-lab/device1/temp' -m '21.5' -q 1

# Publish a retained status, then clear it again with an empty retained message (-n)
mosquitto_pub -h test.mosquitto.org -t 'gimmejob/qa-lab/device1/status' -m 'online' -r
mosquitto_pub -h test.mosquitto.org -t 'gimmejob/qa-lab/device1/status' -r -n

# Receive exactly one message, or give up after 10 seconds: perfect for test scripts
mosquitto_sub -h test.mosquitto.org -t 'gimmejob/qa-lab/device1/temp' -C 1 -W 10

# Hide old retained messages (-R) and show a timestamp, topic and payload for each message
mosquitto_sub -h test.mosquitto.org -t 'gimmejob/qa-lab/#' -R -F '%I %t %p'

# Register a Last Will while subscribing
mosquitto_sub -h test.mosquitto.org -t 'gimmejob/qa-lab/cmd' -i device1 \
  --will-topic 'gimmejob/qa-lab/device1/status' --will-payload 'offline' --will-retain

# Publish a JSON file, use MQTT 5, show every protocol packet (-d)
mosquitto_pub -h test.mosquitto.org -t 'gimmejob/qa-lab/device1/config' -f config.json -V mqttv5 -d

# Broker statistics (Mosquitto brokers)
mosquitto_sub -h test.mosquitto.org -t '$SYS/broker/clients/connected' -C 1 -v
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `-h`, `-p` | Broker host and port (default port 1883) |
| `-t` | Topic. Repeat it to subscribe to several |
| `-m`, `-f`, `-n` | Payload from text, from a file, or empty |
| `-q` | QoS 0, 1 or 2 |
| `-r` | Retain flag (pub) |
| `-v` | Print the topic with each message (sub) |
| `-C n` / `-W s` | Exit after n messages / after s seconds (sub) |
| `-R` | Don't print stale retained messages (sub) |
| `-i` | Client ID |
| `-u`, `-P` | Username and password |
| `--cafile` | CA certificate for TLS. With `-p 8883` and no CA options, Mosquitto 2.x clients load the OS certificates automatically |
| `-V mqttv5` | Use MQTT 5 |
| `-d` | Debug: print CONNECT, CONNACK, PUBLISH and other packets |

> **Caveat:** Ctrl+C makes mosquitto_sub disconnect **cleanly**, so its Last Will is **not** sent. To simulate a crash, kill the process (`kill -9 <pid>`) or cut the network.

## MQTT test scenarios you should run

| Scenario | How to test | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| QoS 1 delivery | Publish with `-q 1` while a subscriber with QoS 1 is connected; watch with `-d` | PUBACK received; duplicates handled idempotently by the consumer |
| Retained state for late joiners | Publish a retained status, then start a new subscriber | New subscriber gets the last value at once |
| Clearing retained state | Publish an empty retained message (`-r -n`) | New subscribers receive nothing |
| Device goes offline | Connect with a Last Will, then kill the process | Observers receive the will (`offline`) |
| Clean disconnect | Disconnect normally | Will is **not** sent; app must publish `offline` itself if needed |
| Offline queue | Subscriber with a fixed client ID and persistent session goes offline; publish QoS 1; reconnect | Queued messages arrive after reconnect |
| Duplicate client ID | Connect two clients with the same `-i` | Broker disconnects the older one; app should report it, not loop forever |
| Authorization (ACL) | Subscribe to `#` or another tenant's topic with a restricted user | Subscription refused (SUBACK failure), no data leak |
| Bad credentials | Wrong password | CONNACK "not authorized" and a clear error in the app |
| Payload robustness | Invalid JSON, empty payload, 1 MB payload, Unicode, wrong types | Consumer rejects or logs safely; no crash |
| Topic validation | Publishing to a topic containing `+` or `#` | Rejected by the client or broker |
| Reconnect behaviour | Restart the broker or drop Wi-Fi | Client reconnects with backoff and resubscribes |

## Debugging MQTT: Wireshark filters, $SYS topics and Postman

- **Wireshark** decodes MQTT on port 1883 automatically. Useful display filters: `mqtt`, `mqtt.msgtype == 1` (CONNECT), `mqtt.msgtype == 3` (PUBLISH), `mqtt.msgtype == 14` (DISCONNECT), `mqtt.topic contains "qa-lab"`, `mqtt.qos == 1`. For port 8883 (TLS) you need the decryption steps from the Wireshark chapter, or a test broker without TLS.
- **`$SYS` topics** on Mosquitto show connected clients, message rates and retained message counts. A sudden jump in `$SYS/broker/clients/connected` during a test often means a reconnect loop.
- **Postman** has an MQTT request type (**Add → MQTT**). It's convenient when the same collection also holds the REST API that triggers device actions.
- **mosquitto_sub -d** prints every MQTT control packet. It's the quickest way to see whether a CONNACK came back with an error code.
- **Exit codes:** when the broker refuses a connection, `mosquitto_pub` and `mosquitto_sub` exit with the CONNACK reason code. For MQTT 3.1.1 that's `4` for a bad username or password and `5` for not authorized; for MQTT 5 it's `134` and `135`. Scripts can assert on `$?`.
- **TLS traffic:** Mosquitto 2.1+ clients accept `--tls-keylog keys.log`. Point Wireshark's TLS *(Pre)-Master-Secret log filename* at that file to read MQTT over port 8883 in clear text. Use this for debugging only.

## Cheat sheet

| Task | How |
| --- | --- |
| See everything under a prefix | `mosquitto_sub -h HOST -t 'prefix/#' -v` |
| Publish once | `mosquitto_pub -h HOST -t topic -m 'payload' -q 1` |
| Set a retained value | `mosquitto_pub ... -r` |
| Clear a retained value | `mosquitto_pub -t topic -r -n` |
| Wait for one message in a script | `mosquitto_sub -t topic -C 1 -W 10` |
| See protocol packets | add `-d` |
| Visual topic tree and history | MQTT Explorer |
| Remove retained topics in bulk | MQTT Explorer → delete branch |
| Device plus observer side by side | MQTTX with two connections |
| Configure a Last Will | MQTTX → Last Will and Testament, or `--will-topic` |
| Inspect on the wire | Wireshark filter `mqtt` |

## Summary

- Know the protocol rules you're testing: topic wildcards, QoS 0/1/2, retained messages, Last Will, persistent sessions and unique client IDs.
- Use MQTT Explorer to see the whole topic tree, history and diffs. Use MQTTX for multi-client scenarios and MQTT 5 options. Use mosquitto_pub / mosquitto_sub for scripts and reproducible bug reports.
- Test the failure paths: crashes that should trigger a Last Will, clean disconnects that shouldn't, duplicate client IDs, ACL violations and bad payloads.
- Use unique topic prefixes and never real data on public brokers. When behaviour is unclear, look at the packets with `-d` or Wireshark.
